Bill.BriefDescription: Conducting a pilot project to provide the fish and wildlife commission with independent biological information.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing the fish and wildlife commission withindependent biological information; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The fish and wildlife commission shallconduct a pilot project designed to provide biological informationdirectly to the commission from a source independent from thedepartment of fish and wildlife. (2) In implementing the pilot project required by this section, thefish and wildlife commission shall contract with private, independentwildlife biologists to prepare an assessment of current elk and deerresource management and recommend future management plans for elk anddeer. The commission shall execute separate contracts for anindependent review of deer and elk management on the area encompassingthe habitat of two individual elk herds a year for five years,beginning with the Mt. St. Helen's elk herd and the Colockum elk herd,and continuing with two different herds each year. (3) The department of fish and wildlife shall, in a timely matter,grant access to any area or provide any information requested by thewildlife biologists that contract with the fish and wildlife commission p. 1 SHB 1250under this section. However, the director of the department of fishand wildlife and other department employees shall have no additionalcontact with the biologists. (4) The results of the initial assessments and plans developedunder this section by the contract wildlife biologists shall bereported directly to the fish and wildlife commission by October 31,2008, with each additional year's information reporting at the end ofthat year. (5) Upon the completion of the pilot project, the chair of the fishand wildlife commission shall present a report to the appropriatecommittees of the legislature on the differences between the managementrecommendations made by the independent biologists as compared torecommendations made by employees of the department of fish andwildlife.
